hypothesis: If weight varies as the cube of a linear dimension during growth, then across childhood and adolescence the population mean body weight scales with the population mean stature with a log-log exponent near 3, so the weight-for-age curve is approximately the cube of the stature-for-age curve.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Data: US NHANES examination data, cycles 2013-2014, 2015-2016 and 2017-2018 (Body Measures BMX_H/I/J and Demographics DEMO_H/I/J XPT files), examined participants aged 2 to 19 years with measured standing height (BMXHT, cm) and weight (BMXWT, kg). For each sex, compute MEC-exam-weighted (WTMEC2YR) mean height and mean weight in 1-year age bins (18 bins), regress log(mean weight) on log(mean height) by ordinary least squares, and also fit the constrained model weight = k * height^3 with k estimated by least squares on the log scale. SUPPORTS if, for both sexes, the free exponent b lies in [2.5, 3.5] AND the cubic model reproduces the age-bin mean weights with R^2 >= 0.90 on the original scale.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if, for either sex, b lies outside [2.5, 3.5] OR the cubic model's R^2 on the age-bin weight curve is < 0.90. MIXED is not possible under this rule except as follows: if the two sexes disagree (one passes, the other fails) the verdict is MIXED. INCONCLUSIVE (data-unavailable) if the files cannot be downloaded.
interpretation: Thompson's 'linear dimension' is measured standing stature and 'weight' is measured body mass, taken as proportional to volume at near-constant density. 'Tend to vary as the cube' is read as an ontogenetic allometric exponent near 3 with a tolerance band of 2.5 to 3.5 because he wrote 'mainly (though not wholly)'. The claim is tested on age-binned population means, which is how he compared the human weight and stature curves, using a modern cross-sectional survey in place of his Quetelet-era tables; survey weights make the means representative of the US population. This follows the swarm thread's draft plan with the cycles fixed in advance.

datasets.name: US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2013-2014, 2015-2016 and 2017-2018: Body Measures (BMX) and Demographics (DEMO) files
datasets.version: public release XPT files as served 2026-10-31
datasets.role: measured standing height and weight with age, sex and MEC exam weights

method: fetch.py downloads six XPT files (16.5 MB). analysis.py merges body measures with demographics per cycle, keeps examined participants aged 2-19 with both measurements, computes MEC-weighted mean height and weight per completed year of age and sex, regresses log mean weight on log mean height (free exponent with 95% CI), fits weight = k * height^3 by least squares on the log scale, and scores the cubic model's R^2 on the original scale.

measured.unit: log-log exponent of mean weight on mean height across ages 2-19, males (pre-registered band 2.5-3.5); females given in extra
measured.n: 4905 males and 4810 females in 18 age bins each

post_hoc_perturbation.reading: The rule passes under the cube law and under exponents inside the pre-registered band, and fails under an exponent of 2 (surface scaling) or 4 at the fractions shown, with the observed heights and the observed bin scatter. The band was pre-registered as a tolerance for Thompson's 'mainly (though not wholly)'; this check shows what it can and cannot reject.

ours_individual_level.ages: 2-19 completed years, standing stature, NHANES 2013-2018 (this test's sample)

theirs.scope: NHANES 2007-2018, ages 0 to 19.99, recumbent length under 24 months, individuals pooled

cross_check.reading: Binning versus individuals is not the cause of the difference: on this test's own sample the individual-level exponent (2.755) is within 0.03 of the age-bin exponents. The cause is the age range. The collaborator's 2-20 year window gives 2.736, which reproduces this test, while their 0-2 year window gives 2.098 and pulls their pooled 0-19 exponent to 2.408, below the 2.5 edge of the band both tests pre-registered. The verdict is therefore conditional on the pre-registered scope (ages 2-19): including infancy makes it 'mixed'.

caveats: The free exponent is below 3 in both sexes (2.74 and 2.86) and the male CI excludes 3, so weight grows a little slower than the cube of stature across childhood; Thompson's 'mainly (though not wholly)' is borne out literally: the cube reproduces the weight curve with R^2 of 0.98-0.99 but is not exact.
Cross-sectional population means from 2013-2018 US children, who are heavier at given height than Thompson's early-20th-century tables; the exponent, not the constant k, is what the claim concerns.
Binned means over 18 ages leave 16 degrees of freedom; the CI reflects bin-to-bin scatter, not individual variation.

Post-hoc discriminating-power check (perturbation.py, added 2026-10-31 after the result; simulation, not observation): with the observed mean heights and bin scatter, the pre-registered rule passes in 100% (males) and 99.95% (females) of 2000 simulations under the cube law, in 0% under an exponent of 2 or 4, and in about 47 to 49% at the band edges 2.5 and 3.5; so the rule rejects surface-law and fourth-power alternatives and is indifferent only at its own pre-registered boundaries.

Cross-check (cross_check.py, added 2026-10-31 after the result; verdict unchanged): the collaborator swarm's test of this claim (origin/main, run cursor/claim-tests-thompson-efb7, NHANES 2007-2018, ages 0 to 19.99 with recumbent length under 24 months) reports a pooled individual-level exponent of 2.408 (95% CI 2.399 to 2.416, n = 23540) and 'mixed'. On this test's own sample the individual-level exponent is 2.755 (CI 2.736 to 2.775, n = 9715; males 2.716, females 2.812), within 0.03 of the age-bin values, so the unit of analysis (bins versus individuals) is not the cause. The cause is the age range: the collaborator's own 2-20 year window gives 2.736 (CI 2.723 to 2.750, n = 19714), reproducing this test, while their 0-2 year window gives 2.098 and pulls the pooled exponent below the 2.5 edge of the band both tests pre-registered. The 'supports' verdict is therefore conditional on the scope fixed at pre-registration (ages 2 to 19, standing stature); including infancy in Thompson's 'during growth' makes it 'mixed'. Whether infancy is inside the claim is a reading of the claim, not a measurement.
